svg.title: Tiel-Coder ties Clef-Flash without thinking, a short think passes it

g.data-text: Tiel-Coder ties Clef-Flash without thinking, a short think passes it
Tiel-Coder with no thinking matches Clef-Flash (−2.1 pp, CI includes 0) at 0.59× its mean latency, both on llama.cpp; ~140 thinking tokens put it +6.6 to +8.2 pp above Clef-Flash at 1.7–1.8 s mean.
mean / p95 / paired 95 % CI vs Clef-Flash (llama.cpp BF16) / think budget, tokens
Callo's pick · no think · 91.0 % / 567 ms mean · p95 817 ms
accuracy and mean latency per decision; a trained head or Clef answers in one pass, without thinking
Data. n = 376 test-s1 (mmlu 80, qnli 80, paws 80, composition_holdout 96, contrastive 40); idle M2 Ultra 64 GB, one at a time; Callo 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-13; Clef 2026-10-09; Kev-9B 2026-10-02.
Timers. Callo arms: --cache on (default); in-Callo frame + read wall time.
Clef arms (2026-10-09). Client wall per request (clef_run.py: a fresh loopback connection, the round trip and JSON parse, one at a time).
Kev-9B (2026-10-02). In-process model forward only (kev.benchmark's LocalPredictor, MPS); tokenisation outside the timer.
Whiskers. Paired 95 % cluster-bootstrap CIs vs Clef-Flash (llama.cpp BF16), stratified by source; dashed line = its accuracy; tails run to each point's p95.
Callo's pick: the fastest point statistically tied with the most accurate (callo compare default, on mean).
Budgets are read from one generation per item, cut at each budget: an item that stops thinking early reads the same at larger budgets, so p50 and p95 can stack.

GiB. File size (GGUF; for native, safetensors shards and head, as shipped); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's counts both shards of its split GGUF, the n-gram shard read lazily from SSD; Kev-9B's counts its base model.

Early exit. Opt-in and experimental in Callo, never picked, so not plotted. At think 256, z .95 with the gate: Tiel-Coder 92.3 % at 1.0 s p50, from a separate calibration whose plain think 256 reads 92.3 % at 1.4 s p50 (the table's run: 92.0 %); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 92.6 % at 2.1 s p50 (its plain think 256: 92.0 % at 5.5 s p50).
Validation. llama.cpp BF16 vs Clef-Flash's release code (2026-10-02 rows): 373/376 argmax agreement, median |Δp| 0.0006 (pre-registered bar 369/376 and 0.010: pass).
Engines. Clef-Flash (release code): 574 ms mean, 2.0× the llama.cpp run's 286 ms; Tiel-Coder without thinking reads 0.29× against it, a gap of engines, not of models.

Builds. Callo 0.3.0 development builds: Tiel-Coder, Dirk, Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma-4-E4B measured on the first build, refit on the refit build; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next measured on the early-exit build, gate reads and profile on the gate-reads build; Sharp-MiniCPM5-2B on the readout-fix build; Tiel-Coder's early-exit calibration on the gate build; llama.cpp b50-4ebdf2c (Callo) and b11379 1537a0a8 (Clef). The first build predates the readout fix; Sharp-MiniCPM5-2B, measured on both sides of it, moved by at most 0.5 pp.
